title: Rotating the hook
description: A wide rotation of the hook moves the target button toward its goal.

title: Ten buttons in 42 actions
description: The robot presses the one button it can reach directly, picks up the stick, and uses it to press the other nine, including the buttons on the table that the robot cannot reach itself. This run solves all 100 held-out instances.

source.selection: Among all 25 StickButton runs (Claude Code with Opus 5 and Codex with GPT-6 Astra in both settings, Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol), the largest held-out instances have 10 buttons; this is the solved 10-button episode with the fewest actions (42).

title: Scooping against the wall
description: The robot regrasps the L-shaped tool, carries it over the wall, and drags it along the floor toward the wall. The wall holds the pile in place, so most of the objects end up in the tool in one large scoop, which the robot lifts over the wall and tips out on the other side.

title: Rescued by the physics
description: The robot gets stuck next to the tool in the corner and repeats the same motion for more than 1,000 steps. Contact slowly shifts the tool until a grasp works, and the robot then carries the balls over the wall in the tool and completes the task in 1,966 steps.

source.selection: Main-setting GPT-6 Astra seed 222 (100%); episode 3 (50 balls) is its longest success. Rendered in a single pass with the policy running, because the taped second pass did not reproduce the success.

title: Pushing the T into place
description: The dot robot pushes the T-shaped block with a sequence of short pushes until it matches the goal pose, here in 104 actions.

source.selection: Main-setting Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol seed 42 (89%); episode 4 is its shortest early success.

title: Clearing two touching obstacles
description: Two obstacles stand 1 mm apart on the target region. This program moves both aside and places the target block. Two other + source programs do not move at all on this instance: one finds no grasp and the other exceeds its own planning time limit.

source.selection: Surprise-catalogue entry on Obstruction3D episode 48 (3 objects), where + source seeds 24 and 444 fail without moving; seed 42 (100%) solves it and is shown.

title: Pairing two triangles into a square
description: The program places two right triangles side by side so that together they form a square next to the square part. The clip ends with a top-down view of the final placement.

source.selection: Run at 79% that solves some but not all 3-part instances; episode 2 is a solved 3-part instance with a cube and two right triangles. Two seconds of a top-down still of the final state are appended.

title: Trying many placements for an equilateral triangle
description: An equilateral triangle cannot be paired into a square. This program tries many positions and orientations until the part fits. The clip ends with a top-down view.

source.selection: A 100% Packing run on episode 11, the same 3-part instance that the 79% run fails. Two seconds of a top-down still of the final state are appended.

title: Catapult-like tossing
description: The robot accelerates the cube into a long toss across the room and into the target bin.

title: Pouring with the tray
description: The robot lifts the source tray and pours its contents directly into the target tray.

title: Retrying failed grasps
description: The program checks what it holds after each lift. Here two stacked cubes come up together, so it releases them and grasps again; later a grasp closes on nothing and it tries again. All four cubes end up in their bins.

source.selection: Claude Code with Opus 5 + source seed 444 (96%). Policy-state logging over its first fourteen 4-cube episodes (0 to 26) found retries only in episode 0 (a two-cube lift at action 68 and an empty grasp at action 395), which is shown at one frame per action.

title: Sweeping with the gripper
description: The robot uses the gripper itself to move cubes into the open drawer.

title: Picking up instead of sweeping
description: The program opens the drawer and grasps the cubes into it rather than sweeping them. It solves all 100 held-out instances.

source.selection: The only GPT-6 Astra SweepIntoDrawer run at 100%; episode 0 is the first held-out instance.

title: Sweeping with the brush
description: The only GPT-6 Astra SweepIntoDrawer program that sweeps: it opens the drawer, picks up the brush, and pushes the cubes toward the drawer. It succeeds here, but on only 15% of instances.

source.selection: Lowest GPT-6 Astra SweepIntoDrawer run (15%), the only one that sweeps; episode 7 is the reviewed success, paired with the episode 0 failure.

title: Carrying cubes one at a time
description: With source access, the program grasps the five cubes one at a time and leaves the sweeping tool unused. It solves every 1- and 5-cube instance and none with 10 or 50 cubes.

source.selection: Best GPT-6 Astra + source SweepSimple run (50%); episode 1 is its first 5-cube instance.

title: Placing blocks on the beam
description: The robot carries the small blocks one at a time and places them on the balance beam. This run solves all 100 held-out instances.

source.selection: Main-setting Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol seed 42 (100%); episode 0 is the first held-out instance.

title: Retrieving an alternative block
description: The program retrieves a block from the far table when the nearby retrieval route is obstructed.

title: Grasping the nearby block from the side
description: The robot moves along the table, clears the obstructing block off the table, and reaches the target block at an awkward angle. The same program solves all 100 held-out instances.

source.selection: Run at 100%. Among the reviewed episodes (0 to 4 and 8), episode 4 shows the nearby-grasp route clearly.

title: Failure: dragging just below a threshold
description: The program drags the target block 2.9999 mm per step, just under the 3 mm it uses to decide the block is being carried, so the carrying phase never starts. The block wedges against its neighbours and the remaining actions are rejected.

source.selection: Codex failure analysis replays this frozen program; episode 22 (3 objects) is the analysed instance in a 27% run.

title: Failure: moving blocks without storing any
description: Three of the seven blocks start in the shelf. The robot moves back and forth across the room, adjusts the stored blocks, and shifts some of the outside blocks a short distance, but never carries an outside block into the shelf. The episode ends at the step limit with the same three blocks stored.

source.selection: Codex failure analysis replays this frozen program; episode 2 (7 objects) is the analysed instance in a 65% run.

title: Failure: repeating a rejected move
description: The program picks a base position inside its own safety margin around the table. With no path there, it falls back to a direct move that collides with the table, and repeats the rejected move for the remaining 899 steps.

source.selection: The single GPT-6 Astra Transport run at 0%; episode 0 is the instance diagnosed with per-step collision checks (one accepted base move, then 899 moves rejected for a table collision).

title: Failure: searching a grid of base positions
description: The program has no model of the arm. It tries a grid of base positions around the box with a few fixed arm poses, looking for one where the grasp works, and is still searching when the step limit ends the episode. This run scores 0%.

source.selection: Main-setting Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol seed 42 (0%); episode 0 is the first held-out instance (one cube and the box).

title: Failure: no rule for equilateral triangles
description: The same program as the triangle-pairing example, on an instance with two equilateral triangles. It places the parts in a row, two of them hang over the edges of the rack, and the robot then waits until the step limit. The clip ends with a top-down view.

source.selection: Same 79% run as the triangle-pairing success; episode 11 is the 3-part instance that the 100% run solves by trying many placements. Two seconds of a top-down still of the final state are appended.

title: Three rods on the lower shelves
description: Three rods fit on the lower shelves, and this program places all of them. It solves most instances with one, two, three, or five objects.

source.selection: Best GPT-6 Astra ConstrainedCupboard run (63%); episode 2 is a solved 3-object instance, paired with its 4-object failure.

title: Failure: a fourth rod needs a higher shelf
description: The same program on a four-rod instance. Only three rods fit on the lower shelves, so the fourth needs a higher shelf, which this program never uses. It fails every 4- and 6-object instance.

source.selection: Same run as the 3-object success (63%); episode 3 is its first 4-object instance. This run solves 0/17 4-object and 0/16 6-object instances; the 28% run (seed 424) is the only GPT-6 Astra run that solves 4-object instances (13/17).

title: Using the higher shelves
description: The same four-rod instance, solved by Claude Code with Opus 5 + source. This program places rods on the higher shelves when the lower ones are full and solves all 100 held-out instances, so the 4- and 6-object instances are solvable.

source.selection: Claude Code + source run at 100%; episode 3 is the same 4-object held-out instance as the GPT-6 Astra failure (Astra seed 42, episode 3).

title: Failure: sweeping without coordination
description: The same sweeping program on another instance. Some cubes reach the drawer, but others stay on the counter or are pushed off, and the 1,000-step limit ends the episode.

source.selection: Same run as the brush-sweeping success; episode 0 is the first held-out instance and fails.

title: Failure: the drawer is never opened
description: The program pushes the cubes over the counter edge, but it never opens the drawer, so they fall to the floor. The gripper then stays at the drawer front until the step limit. No main-setting Claude Code run solves SweepIntoDrawer.

source.selection: Main-setting Claude Code seed 444 (0%); episode 0 matches the GPT-6 Astra SweepIntoDrawer cards.

title: Failure: dropping the tray
description: The program lifts the source tray to turn it over above the target tray. On this 20-cube instance, the robot loses the loaded tray at the edge of the table and cannot recover it.

source.selection: Main-setting GPT-6 Astra seed 424 (22%); episode 6 is a 20-cube failure among the reviewed episodes (0, 1, 6).

title: Failure: cubes between the trays
description: The robot lifts the yellow tray and tips it over the green tray. Most cubes fall in, but a few land on the table between the trays, and the program does not pick them up.

source.selection: Main-setting Claude Code seed 424; episode 35 is a 10-cube failure in a run that solves most 10-cube instances.

title: Failure: cubes left at the shelf mouth
description: The robot lifts each cube toward the top shelf, but every cube drops and the three end up in a row on the floor in front of the shelf. This run solves some one- and two-cube instances (22% overall) and none with three or more.

source.selection: Main-setting Claude Code run at 22% (count 1: 9/17, count 2: 13/17, 3 or more: 0); episode 2 is a 3-cube failure. The same held-out instance is solved by the seed 424 run.

title: Failure: fixed joint poses
description: The program moves the arm through a short list of fixed joint poses instead of computing them from the cube's position. The arm cycles between these poses and the cube never reaches the shelf. This run scores 0%.

source.selection: Main-setting Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol seed 424 (0%, Codex Reruns collection); episode 0 is a one-cube instance.

title: Failure: knocking both objects over
description: The task is to put the boxed drink and the can next to the bowl. The gripper knocks the boxed drink over on its way past, then tips the can onto its side while grasping it. The robot stays over the fallen can for the rest of the episode.

source.selection: Main-setting Claude Code seed 424; episode 0 is the first held-out instance.

title: Failure: cycling through the bins
description: Main-setting GPT-6 Astra programs assign cubes to bins by cycling through the four bins in the order the cubes appear in the state. That matches the goal with four cubes but not with twenty, so no twenty-cube instance can succeed. In this episode the robot also pushes the bins out of place. The clip shows every fourth action.

source.selection: Main-setting GPT-6 Astra seed 42 (50%: all 4-cube instances, no 20-cube instance); episode 1 is its first 20-cube instance.
